item.title: National economy remained steady with innovation-led and high-quality development in August
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-15
National Bureau of Statistics of China 15 September, 2026 In August, under the strong leadership of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China (CPC) with Comrade Xi Jinping at its core, all regions and departments fully implemented the decisions and arrangements made by the CPC Central Committee and the State Council, adhered to the general principle of pursuing progress while ensuring stability, strived to make the macro policies more effective, deepened the reform and opening up, accelerated the transition from traditional growth drivers to new ones, and pursued high-quality development. As a result, production and supply grew steadily, employment and prices were generally stable, foreign trade witnessed rapid growth, and new growth drivers played a stronger underpinning role. The national economy maintained the steady momentum with innovation-led and high-quality development. 1. Industrial Production Accelerated and Equipment Manufacturing and High-Tech Manufacturing Grew Fast. In August, the total value added of industrial enterprises above the designated size grew by 5.2 percent year on year, 0.7 percentage points faster than that of last month, or grew by 0.54 percent month on month. In terms of sectors, the value added of mining decreased by 1.4 percent year on year, that of manufacturing grew by 6.1 percent, and that of production and supply of electricity, heat power, gas and water went up by 4.9 percent. The value added of equipment manufacturing increased by 12.1 percent year on year and that of high-tech manufacturing increased by 16.7 percent, 6.9 percentage points and 11.5 percentage points faster than that of the industrial enterprises above the designated size respectively. An analysis by types of ownership showed that the value added of state holding enterprises was up by 3.0 percent year on year; that of share-holding enterprises was up by 5.7 percent; that of enterprises funded by foreign investors or investors from Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan was up by 3.4 percent; and that of private enterprises was up by 3.7 percent. In terms of products, the production of lithium-ion batteries, industrial robots and 3D printing devices grew by 57.2 percent, 34.6 percent and 29.9 percent year on year respectively. In the first eight months, the value added of industrial enterprises above the designated size went up by 5.3 percent year on year. In August, the Manufacturing Purchasing Managers’ Index stood at 49.8 percent and the Production and Operation Expectation Index was 53.8 percent. In the first seven months, the total profits made by industrial enterprises above the designated size were 4,582.1 billion yuan, up by 17.6 percent year on year. 2. Service Sector Grew Steadily and Modern Services Showed Good Momentum of Growth. In August, the Index of Services Production grew by 4.1 percent year on year. Specifically, that of information transmission, software and information technology services, leasing and business services, and transport, storage and postal services grew by 9.6 percent, 9.0 percent and 4.8 percent year on year respectively. In the first eight months, the Index of Services Production increased by 4.7 percent year on year. In August, the Business Activity Index for Services stood at 49.3 percent and the Business Activity Expectation Index for Services was 55.5 percent. Among which, the Business Activity Index for post, telecommunication, broadcast, television and satellite transmission services, and internet software and information technology services stayed within the high expansion range of 55.0 percent and above. In the first seven months, the business revenue of service enterprises above the designated size grew by 5.7 percent year on year. 3. Market Sales Scaled Up and Service Retails Saw Fast Growth. In the first eight months, the total retail sales of goods and services grew by 2.5 percent year on year. Specifically, the retail sales of services increased by 4.9 percent and that of goods increased by 1.0 percent. In terms of retail sales of services, that of communication information services, tourism consultation and rental services, and cultural, sports and leisure services grew fast. In the first eight months, the total retail sales of consumer goods reached 32,756.9 billion yuan, up by 1.1 percent year on year. In the first eight months, the online retail sales of goods and services reached 13,476.6 billion yuan, up by 4.6 percent year on year. Specifically, the online retail sales of goods were 8,419.5 billion yuan, up by 4.3 percent, and the online retail sales of services totaled 5,057.1 billion yuan, up by 5.1 percent. In August, the total retail sales of consumer goods reached 3,982.4 billion yuan, up by 0.4 percent year on year, or down by 0.13 percent month on month. Analyzed by different areas, the retail sales of consumer goods in urban areas reached 3,445.7 billion yuan, up by 0.2 percent year on year, and that in rural areas stood at 536.7 billion yuan, up by 1.6 percent. Grouped by consumption patterns, the retail sales of goods were 3,528.0 billion yuan, up by 0.3 percent; the income of catering was 454.4 billion yuan, up by 1.1 percent. Sales of basic living goods and certain upgraded goods enjoyed fast growth. The retail sales of beverages, of grain, oil and food, and of communication equipment by enterprises above the designated size went up by 4.9 percent, 4.0 percent and 27.3 percent year on year respectively. 4. Investment in Fixed Assets Declined and Investment in Intellectual Property Products Grew Fast. In the first eight months, the investment in fixed assets (excluding rural households) reached 29,309.2 billion yuan, down by 7.2 percent year on year; the investment in fixed assets was down by 4.2 percent with the investment in real estate development deducted. Specifically, the investment in intellectual property products increased by 9.2 percent year on year. The investment in high-tech industries grew by 5.2 percent year on year, of which the investment in information services, aerospace vehicle and equipment manufacturing, and electronic and communication equipment manufacturing grew by 22.7 percent, 14.9 percent and 6.9 percent respectively. By industry, the investment in the primary industry went down by 2.4 percent year on year, that in the secondary industry down by 2.9 percent, and that in the tertiary industry down by 9.9 percent. In terms of sectors, the investment in infrastructure declined by 4.0 percent year on year; that in manufacturing was down by 2.3 percent; and that in real estate development declined by 19.9 percent. The private investment went down by 10.1 percent year on year, or down by 6.4 percent with the investment in real estate development deducted. The floor space of newly-built commercial buildings sold was 498.80 million square meters, down by 12.1 percent year on year; the total sales of newly-built commercial buildings were 4,747.0 billion yuan, down by 13.0 percent. The floor space of second-hand housing online transactions reached 549.23 million square meters, an increase of 10.6 percent year on year. In August, the investment in fixed assets (excluding rural households) declined by 0.50 percent month on month. 5. Imports and Exports of Goods Grew Fast and Trade Structure Continued to Optimize. In August, the total value of imports and exports of goods was 4,645.5 billion yuan, an increase of 19.8 percent year on year, 0.6 percentage points faster than that of the previous month. Specifically, the total value of exports was 2,727.4 billion yuan, up by 18.6 percent; the total value of imports was 1,918.1 billion yuan, up by 21.7 percent. In the first eight months, the total value of imports and exports of goods reached 34,775.3 billion yuan, up by 17.6 percent year on year. Specifically, the total value of exports was 20,165.8 billion yuan, up by 14.6 percent. The total value of imports was 14,609.5 billion yuan, up by 22.0 percent. In the first eight months, the imports and exports of general trade increased by 10.5 percent year on year. The imports and exports with the Belt and Road partner countries grew by 15.9 percent. The imports and exports by private enterprises increased by 17.6 percent. The exports of mechanical and electrical products grew by 21.9 percent. 6. Employment was Generally Stable and Urban Surveyed Unemployment Rate Saw Seasonal Increase. In the first eight months, the urban surveyed unemployment rate averaged 5.2 percent, maintaining the same level as that of the same period last year. In August, the urban surveyed unemployment rate was 5.3 percent, 0.1 percentage points higher than that of the previous month. The surveyed unemployment rate of population with local household registration was 5.3 percent and that of population with non-local household registration was 5.2 percent, of which, the rate of population with non-local agricultural household registration stood at 5.0 percent. The urban surveyed unemployment rate in 31 major cities was 5.3 percent, 0.1 percentage points higher than that of the previous month. The employees of enterprises worked 48.2 hours per week on average. 7. Consumer Price Rose Mildly and Producer Prices for Industrial Products Grew Faster Year on Year. In August, the consumer price index (CPI) increased by 0.8 percent year on year, 0.3 percentage points higher than that of the previous month, or up by 0.4 percent month on month. Grouped by commodity categories, prices for food, tobacco, alcohol and dining out went down by 0.7 percent year on year; clothing up by 1.3 percent; housing down by 0.3 percent; articles and services for daily use up by 0.7 percent; transportation and communication up by 2.5 percent; education, culture and recreation up by 1.4 percent; medical services and health care up by 2.7 percent; and other articles and services up by 7.3 percent. In terms of prices for food, tobacco, alcohol and dining out, the price for pork went down by 11.8 percent, fresh vegetables down by 2.8 percent, grain down by 0.6 percent, and fresh fruits down by 0.5 percent. The core CPI excluding the prices of food and energy went up by 1.0 percent year on year. In the first eight months, the CPI went up by 0.9 percent year on year. In August, the producer prices for industrial products went up by 3.8 percent year on year, 0.3 percentage points faster than that of the previous month, or up by 0.4 percent month on month. The purchasing prices for industrial producers went up by 5.8 percent year on year, or up by 0.3 percent month on month. In the first eight months, the producer prices for industrial products and the purchasing prices for industrial producers rose by 2.0 percent and 3.2 percent year on year respectively. Generally speaking, in August, the national economy was generally stable, featuring innovation-led growth and better structure. However, we should be aware that the adverse impact of external environment has intensified, the domestic imbalance between strong supply and weak demand is still acute, some enterprises are facing difficulties in their operations and the foundation for steady and upward economic growth still needs to be consolidated. At the next stage, we must follow the guidance of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, adhere to the general principle of pursuing progress while ensuring stability, fully and faithfully apply the new development philosophy on all fronts, and move faster to foster a new pattern of development. We must deepen the reform and opening up, step up macro-policy adjustment, boost domestic demands, advance the industrial upgrading, and strengthen the development momentum while boosting the social vitality, so as to sustain the positive momentum of innovation-led and high-quality economic development. Notes: 1. The growth rates of value added of industrial enterprises above the designated size and its sub-items are calculated at comparable prices. Both are real growth rates. The growth rates of other indicators are nominal growth by using current prices unless otherwise specified. 2. Industrial enterprises above the designated size are industrial enterprises with annual revenue from principal business over 20 million yuan. As industrial enterprises above the designated size change every year, to ensure the data comparability between years, the coverage of the data of the same period last year used for estimating year-on-year growth rates like that of products output, is as consistent as possible with the current period and different from the coverage of the data published last year. The main reasons are as follows: First, the statistical units change. Every year, some enterprises are included in the survey as they meet the threshold, while some enterprises are removed from the survey because of downsizing. Besides, enterprises that have newly gone into operation, been bankrupted, canceled their registrations or had their business licenses revoked also cause impact. Second, duplicated outputs across regions of enterprise groups have been removed based on the ad hoc surveys since duplication is found in the products output of some enterprise groups. 3. The Index of Services Production is the change of production in the reporting period compared to the base period with the price factors deducted. 4. Total retail sales of goods and services refer to the total value of goods and services provided directly by enterprises (businesses, self-employed units) to other units and individuals for non-production and non-operating purposes in the form of transactions. It consists of retail sales of goods and retail sales of services. The retail sales of goods directly adopt the corresponding figure from the total retail sales of consumer goods, reflecting the development and changes in the goods consumption market. The retail sales of services refer to the total value of services directly provided by enterprises (businesses, self-employed units) to other units and individuals for non-production and non-operating purposes in the form of transactions, reflecting the development and changes in the services consumption market. The scope of the total retail sales of consumer goods includes all legal entities, establishments and self-employed units involved in retail trades or providing catering services. Specifically, businesses above the designated size include wholesale enterprises (businesses, self-employed units), retail enterprises (businesses, self-employed units) and lodging and catering enterprises (businesses, self-employed units) with annual revenue from principal business over 20 million yuan, 5 million yuan and 2 million yuan respectively. As the wholesale, retail, and lodging and catering enterprises (businesses, self-employed units) above the designated size change every year, to ensure the data comparability between years, the coverage of the data of the same period last year used for estimating year-on-year growth rates like that of the retail sales of consumer goods by businesses above the designated size is consistent with the current period and different from the coverage of data published last year. The main reasons are: some enterprises (businesses, self-employed units) are included in the survey as they meet the threshold, while some enterprises (businesses, self-employed units) are removed from the survey because of downsizing every year. Besides, enterprises (businesses, self-employed units) that have newly gone into operation, been bankrupted, canceled their registrations or had their business licenses revoked also cause impact. 5. To reflect the development of the online consumption market in a more comprehensive way, the statistical indicators for online consumption have been improved with the coverage of the online service platforms expanded to strengthen the measurement of the online services retail sales in line with the evolving momentum of online consumption. Accordingly, the original indicator “online retail sales” has been adjusted to “online retail sales of goods and services”, with the definition unchanged and the statistical coverage expanded. The indicator “online retail sales of physical goods” has been adjusted to “online retail sales of goods,” with the definition and statistical coverage unchanged. In addition, “online retail sales of services” has been introduced as a new indicator. The online retail sales of goods and services are not comparable with the online retail sales. As the coverage of key platforms included in the statistics of online retail sales of goods and services changes every year, to ensure the comparability of data between years, the data coverage for the same period last year used for estimating the year-on-year growth rates of online retail sales of goods and services is consistent with that of the current period and differs from the data coverage released last year. The main reasons are as follows: new platforms are included in the survey every year , while platforms that no longer meet the requirements of the statistical programs are removed from the survey. 6. Investment in fixed assets (excluding rural households) refers to the workload and related costs for the construction and acquisition of fixed assets completed within a certain period of time, expressed in monetary terms. According to the current statistical programs, investment in infrastructure includes investment in fixed assets in the following industries: production and supply of electricity and heat, production and supply of gas, production and supply of water, railway transportation, road transportation, water transportation, air transportation, pipeline transport, multi-modal transportation and forwarding agency, loading, unloading and delivery, postal services, telecommunications, radio, TV and satellite transmission services, internet and related services, water conservancy management, ecological conservation and environmental governance, and management of public facilities. The growth rate of investment in infrastructure is calculated on a comparable basis. Investment in intellectual property products refers to the investment completed in the reporting period for the production and acquisition of intellectual property products. It mainly includes investment in computer software and databases, research and development, mineral exploration and evaluation, and entertainment, literary and artistic originals. According to the reform of the statistical program and methodology of investment and the requirements of statistical law enforcement, the data of investment in fixed assets of the same period last year have been revised. The growth rates of investment in fixed assets are calculated on a comparable basis. 7. Data of second-hand housing transactions are from the Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development. 8. Data of imports and exports are from the General Administration of Customs. 9. Due to the rounding-off reasons, the subentries may not add up to the aggregate totals. In case of any differences between English translation and the original Chinese text, the Chinese edition shall prevail.

item.title: Xi's article on advancing basic research to be published
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-15
BEIJING, Sept. 15 -- An article by Xi Jinping, general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee, on strengthening basic research will be published on Wednesday. The article by Xi, also Chinese president and chairman of the Central Military Commission, will be published in this year's 18th issue of the Qiushi Journal, a flagship magazine of the CPC Central Committee. Noting that basic research is the bedrock of the entire scientific system and a frontier area of global sci-tech competition, the article emphasizes further efforts to develop the country's basic research to build China into a leading country in science and technology. Compared with global leaders in science and technology, China still lags behind in basic research, the article says, calling for stronger efforts and more concrete measures to strengthen basic research, enhance the country's capacity for original innovation, and accelerate efforts toward greater self-reliance and strength in science and technology. The layout of basic research should be optimized, with the main directions and priority areas for basic research further clarified based on the country's urgent and long-term needs, the article says. It also underscores the importance of promoting coordinated development of applied disciplines and basic disciplines, while encouraging integration among different disciplines and interdisciplinary research. The article calls for efforts to expand the basic research talent pool and provide greater support for young talent. It also stresses the importance of inspiring the imagination and curiosity of young people, so that more of them will regard pursuing basic research as a lifelong aspiration. On ramping up support for basic research, the article calls for gradually raising the proportion of funding for basic research while strengthening the systematic development of major scientific and technological infrastructure. Attention should also be paid to AI-empowered basic research and the development of a system of intelligent research platforms, it adds. The article also urges the country's active integration into the global innovation network, boosting original innovation capacity through openness and cooperation. It also emphasizes the need to further open up national science and technology programs, take the lead in initiating and participating in international big science programs and projects, and take an active part in global scientific and technological governance.

item.title: Xi urges Chinese police to remain committed to serving people with responsibility, dedication
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-15
BEIJING, Sept. 15 -- Chinese President Xi Jinping has called on the country's police officers to remain committed to serving the people, be loyal guardians of the Party and the people, and demonstrate a strong sense of responsibility and dedication. Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the remarks in a reply letter to a primary-level police force from Zhangzhou, east China's Fujian Province. In his letter to the "Zhangzhou 110" police unit, Xi lauded its police officers for their dedication and hard work at the grassroots level in serving the public and maintaining social stability for the people. He emphasized that the police bear the important responsibility of safeguarding the people's well-being and the country's peace, calling on Chinese police to uphold fine traditions, devote themselves to wholeheartedly addressing the needs and concerns of the people, and work diligently to protect the safety of the public. The "Zhangzhou 110" unit is one of the exemplary primary-level units within China's police forces. Since 1990, it has pioneered and continuously improved a rapid response mechanism tied to the 110 police emergency call service, playing a significant role in combating crime, maintaining public security, and serving the community. During his tenure in Fujian, Xi visited the police unit three times to inspect and guide its work. Recently, members of the unit wrote to Xi, reporting on their work and expressing their determination to fulfill duties on the new journey.

item.title: China unveils measures to boost smart home consumption
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-14
BEIJING, Sept. 14 -- China on Monday unveiled an action plan to further promote smart home consumption by enriching application scenarios and expanding high-quality supply. The plan, jointly issued by eight government departments including the Ministry of Commerce, the National Development and Reform Commission and the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, also calls for supporting elderly-friendly renovation and smart upgrading of older homes while better meeting the consumption needs of different groups. The plan sets out seven measures to expand high-quality smart home supply, improve the smart home standards system, support smart home consumption, develop elderly-friendly smart home products, streamline the service chain for recycling used household goods, optimize community services, and strengthen fiscal and financial support. To expand supply, the plan encourages manufacturers to step up research and development of smart home products and supports home furnishing stores and shopping malls in setting up smart home experience centers and model rooms for whole-home smart systems and digital homes. On standards, it calls for improving the grading and evaluation standards system for smart home products and accelerating the formulation and implementation of mandatory national standards on connectivity and interoperability. To support consumption, the plan encourages local authorities to determine eligible smart home product categories and subsidy standards based on local conditions under China's 2026 consumer goods trade-in policy. Under this year's consumer goods trade-in policy, local governments have greater flexibility in designing subsidy programs. The country plans to allocate 250 billion yuan (about 36.93 billion U.S. dollars) in ultra-long special treasury bond funds to support the nationwide program.

item.title: Xi calls on BRICS to unite Global South, deepen cooperation
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-14
NEW DELHI, Sept. 13 -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Sunday called on BRICS countries to strengthen unity among the Global South and play an active, stabilizing and positive role in global affairs. In a speech when attending the second day of BRICS summit in New Delhi, Xi also outlined concrete proposals to further strengthen greater BRICS cooperation, with a focus on emerging areas including artificial intelligence, trade, digital industries and manufacturing. KEY DRIVER OF MULTIPOLARITY Xi pointed out that when changes unseen in a century are accelerating across the world, the Global South, with its collective rise, has become a key driver of world multipolarity. At the same time, the international landscape is volatile and fraught with risks and challenges, Xi said, adding that to bring stability to the world and make it a better place, BRICS countries must seize the historical initiative, rally the Global South, and advance the well-being of all humanity. Global South countries should jointly defend the rule of law in international affairs, safeguard the basic norms of international relations including sovereign equality, noninterference in internal affairs, and the peaceful settlement of disputes, Xi said. It should be ensured that international law and international rules are applied to all, and free from double standards, he added. Global South countries should hold high the banner of multilateralism, uphold the authority and role of the United Nations, and support multilateral institutions in advancing reform and increasing efficiency, Xi said. He also called for promoting the reform of the World Trade Organization in the right direction, as well as reforming and improving the international financial architecture to increase the representation and voice of developing countries. Global South countries should stay committed to a people-centered development philosophy and strive to deliver on the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, Xi said. Global South countries should also jointly advance security governance, tackle both traditional and nontraditional security threats, and improve global climate governance, Xi said, also calling for working faster to evolve a consensus-based global AI governance framework, so that new technologies can light the way toward shared prosperity. "It is a solidarity that unlocks partnerships, unlocks democratization of the international system, unlocks an open international system, and unlocks an inclusive international system," said Charles Onunaiju, director of the Center for China Studies in Nigeria. Rakhim Oshakbayev, director of the TALAP Center for Applied Research in Kazakhstan and former Kazakh vice minister for investment and development, said BRICS cooperation should "bring together developing countries' shared aspirations and promote coordination and cooperation." BRICS countries should continue seeking common interests, he said, noting that the grouping's expansion had placed greater demands on internal coordination. GREATER BRICS COOPERATION During the speech, Xi proposed five initiatives on "greater BRICS" cooperation in areas of AI, trade and investment facilitation, digital industry, intelligent manufacturing, and science and technology talent development. To accomplish great things and achieve major progress, the foundation of greater BRICS cooperation must be cemented, Xi said, calling for leveraging BRICS' close ties with fellow emerging markets and Global South countries, upholding open cooperation for mutual benefit, safeguarding stable and smooth industrial and supply chains, and fostering a large integrated market. "We should build incubators for innovation, upgrade traditional industries, develop emerging industries, and deploy future industries," Xi said. On the open source and inclusive AI initiative, Xi said that China will be a pioneer in establishing a BRICS AI open source community, support the cooperation in developing and applying large language models, hold specialized AI seminars and training courses, and build an open ecosystem for AI. On the trade and investment facilitation initiative, China proposes to establish a BRICS special economic zone partnership, under which countries can set up an intelligent portal, coordinate policies, and build a new frontier for open development, Xi said, adding that in an effort to cultivate new drivers of economic and trade cooperation, China will hold the BRICS Forum on Trade in Services next year. On the digital industry cooperation initiative, Xi said that China will push for establishing a BRICS digital ecosystem cloud platform, and conduct digital skills training, technological exchange and industrial alignment, so as to jointly enable the development of the digital economy. On the intelligent manufacturing cooperation initiative, China stands ready to assist fellow BRICS countries in building smart factories and developing standards and norms, and jointly promote manufacturing transformation and upgrading, he said. On the science and technology talent development initiative, China proposes to set up a BRICS engineer cultivation alliance for joint development of engineers and mutual recognition of competency standards, Xi said, adding that China will launch a BRICS youth exchange program for scientific and technological innovation, so as to cultivate more high-caliber talent. The five initiatives proposed by Xi focus on key areas including technology, industry, trade and talent, providing concrete pathways to lay a solid foundation for practical cooperation among the broader BRICS community, said Serik Korzhumbayev, editor-in-chief of the Delovoy Kazakhstan newspaper. It demonstrates China's firm resolve to share the opportunities of its modernization, a reflection of the spirit of openness, inclusiveness and mutual benefit that underpins BRICS cooperation, he said.

item.title: Chinese premier chairs State Council executive meeting
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-12
BEIJING, Sept. 11 -- Chinese Premier Li Qiang on Friday chaired a State Council executive meeting to make further arrangements on ensuring workplace safety. Workplace safety accidents have occurred frequently in recent times, with profound lessons to be learned, the meeting said. It urged an in-depth investigation into the causes of these accidents and strong measures to address the problems identified. Efforts should be made to further tighten workplace safety responsibilities and address risks and potential hazards in key industries and areas, it said. Any violations of laws and regulations must be dealt with resolutely to firmly uphold the bottom line of workplace safety, effectively curb major accidents, and safeguard people's lives and property, according to the meeting. The meeting also reviewed progress on developing computing networks and upgrading aging reservoirs. Computing networks provide the fundamental support for the development of artificial intelligence, the meeting said, calling for efforts to improve computing infrastructure and actively advance the research, development and application of key technologies and equipment. Coordinated development of computing capacity and electricity supply, as well as the integration of computing and communications networks, should be promoted, said the meeting. The role of market mechanisms should be better leveraged to support enterprises in technological innovation and application as well as resource integration, it added. The meeting stressed the need to comprehensively improve the safety of aging reservoirs and make their renovation and upgrading more targeted and effective. Noting the achievements over the past year in elevating China to a leading country in education, the meeting called for the appropriate allocation of educational resources in response to changes in the school-age population to better meet the needs arising from enrollment peaks at different stages of education. To meet national strategic needs, efforts should focus on cultivating outstanding innovative talent, continuously optimizing the structure of academic disciplines and majors, strengthening the development of textbook systems, and improving talent training models, according to the meeting. The meeting also advocated for a health-first approach to education, aiming to promote students' physical and mental well-being as well as their all-round development. The meeting also reviewed and approved a draft revision to the Regulation on the Administration of Foundations. Greater efforts should be made to strengthen the credibility of foundations, further standardize their management and improve relevant systems, so as to promote the sound and orderly development of China's public interest activities and charities, it said.

item.title: China willing to help advance global energy security, sustainable development: vice premier
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-11
BEIJING, Sept. 10 -- China is willing to work with all parties to advance global energy security and sustainable development, Chinese Vice Premier Ding Xuexiang said Thursday. Ding, also a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, made the remarks while delivering a speech at the opening ceremony of the 16th Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Energy Ministerial Meeting in Beijing. China will always defend the stability of global energy markets, contribute to the global green and low-carbon transition, and participate in international energy cooperation, Ding said. The vice premier noted that China has been actively engaged in pragmatic energy cooperation within the APEC framework, effectively promoting regional energy development, and making important contributions to safeguarding global energy security. To advance global energy security and sustainable development, Ding urged efforts to vigorously develop distributed energy sources and charging infrastructure to enhance inclusive energy development in the Asia-Pacific region. Ding also called for conducting collaborative research and development on emerging technologies such as new energy storage and digital grids, and promoting mature technologies and application scenarios to better empower the energy transition in the Asia-Pacific region. It is necessary to ensure the stable operation of energy industrial and supply chains and facilitate the smooth functioning of regional and global energy markets, Ding added.

item.title: China tightens accountability for officials regarding ecological, environmental damage
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-26
BEIJING, Aug. 25 -- Chinese officials found responsible for serious ecological and environmental damage will be held accountable for life, even if they have since left their posts, according to a recently released policy document. Issued by the General Office of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and the General Office of the State Council, the document outlines the cases that can lead to official accountability, as well as the disciplinary measures that may follow. The accountability framework was originally released in 2015. An official with the Organization Department of the CPC Central Committee said an update was necessary as China has entered a stage of high-quality development featuring accelerated green and low-carbon growth, while the CPC Central Committee has issued a series of new requirements on ecological and environmental protection in recent years. The revised rules broaden the scope of accountability beyond leading Party and government officials to include senior officials at public institutions, development zones and state-owned enterprises. China has pledged to bring carbon dioxide emissions to a peak before 2030 and achieve carbon neutrality before 2060. The revised document specifies that local officials who fail to effectively advance these efforts will also be held accountable. Meanwhile, the official from the Organization Department of the CPC Central Committee noted that accountability for ecological and environmental damage must be precise and evidence-based. "It should neither dampen officials' enthusiasm for work, nor undermine the credibility of the Party and the government." China has stepped up ecological and environmental protection efforts. During the second round of the central ecological and environmental protection inspections, conducted from May 2020 to June 2022, a total of 3,371 people were held accountable. The third round of such inspections is currently underway. The revised accountability rules also bring them into line with China's Ecological and Environmental Code, which officially took effect on Aug. 15.
